geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the dominant mass from a single cantilevered block into a split-wing figure so the ground plane can register a public void or entry seam on the access side.
Split along the long axis to preserve a clear dominant gesture while creating a more legible street-facing opening.
Maintain continuity through a grounded spine so the two wings remain one building and do not read as colliding volumes.
Create a modest void large enough to read publicly, but not so large that the solid fragments lose hierarchy.
Keep the mass compact and capacity-aware while allowing the upper figure to remain calm.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the simple cantilever emphasis with a split-wing massing to create a clearer ground-level public threshold and reduce box-like enclosure.
Use the long axis split to open the mass toward the verified access edge.
Add a grounded connector so the split produces a legible entry seam rather than two isolated fragments.
Keep the mass unified across views while still allowing a public void below or between the wings.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent four-view mass with a readable dominant block and some stepped/canted upper articulation, but the public edge is weak: the blue frontage edge is not answered by a clear court, notch, seam, or undercut, and the form largely behaves as a compact stacked object rather than a neighborhood building with an active ground threshold. It is coherent in all views, so there is no view-to-view collision failure, but the visible program relation is only partial. The silhouette is acceptable as an early massing study, yet the form remains too box-like and the void logic is underdeveloped for neighborhood living. The reference set suggests two transferable directions: preserve the stepped/tapered dominant gesture from the mixed-use tower precedent, and carve a more explicit public void/threshold from the atrium precedent, ideally aligned to the verified access edge. As shown, the mass does not hard-fail on repair or continuity, but it does fail program_fit_hard_pass because the ground/public condition is semantically too muted.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office atrium logic may not map directly to neighborhood living unless the ground threshold and access edge stay active.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A carved central void can organize a compact block and create a legible interior public figure.

warnings: The verified primary access edge appears to be answered only indirectly; no clear west-facing public threshold is visible in the massing.
The candidate reads as a single compact object more than a neighborhood living building with an active ground condition.
Stepped upper geometry is coherent, but it should not be mistaken for an adequate public/sectional response.
